# A unique minimizing buffered cap with an unavoidable inside facet

This is an actual fixed-mark counterexample to selecting an inside-free
minimizing buffered cap. the contributor proposed the family; the all-normal proof
below uses disjoint symmetric cores and elementary strip clipping.
The source is NOT claimed to be globally deepest or a joint bad minimum.
The invariant buffer parameter is a definite positive number, not an
arbitrarily-small-parameter family. No OC conclusion is claimed.

## 1. Actual compatible, strictly nonheavy fibers and invariant buffer

Let n=1,d=2 and P={-2,-1,0,1,2}. Use continuous coordinates (x,y) and

    r_(-2),r_(-1),r_0,r_1,r_2=(1,5,5,4,3),
    K_z=[-r_z/2,r_z/2] times [-1,1].                       (1)

The successive radius differences 4,0,-1,-1 are nonincreasing. Thus the
piecewise-affine concave interpolation r(z) defines the ACTUAL convex body

    C={-2<=z<=2, |x|<=r(z)/2, |y|<=1}

with exactly these positive integer fibers. Their volumes are
(2,10,10,8,6), total M=36. Every fiber is strictly lighter than M/2=18.
Every proper closed-minor count quota is strict: singletons have mass<18;
every closed minor containing at least two sites is a consecutive chain
with both parities and, when proper, mass<36.

The within-fiber covariance average is

    Sigma=diag(19/12,1/3).                                 (2)

Indeed sum r=18 and sum r^3=342, so Sigma_xx=342/(12*18).
Set Y=(0,0,1/2), f=(E_K0(0,1/2)/36)^(1/3), L=1, and choose

    epsilon=sqrt(3)/(2f).                                  (3)

This is a positive finite invariant-buffer parameter. Explicitly the
source energy is 115/32+65 sqrt(13)/64. To verify it, symmetry and
convexity make the optimizing horizontal energy parameter zero. The
remaining energy is

    80(2-c)/[(2-3c)^2(2+c)^2], -2<c<2/3,

whose unique minimizer is c=(10-4sqrt(13))/9. Formula(3) is approximately
1.4771. In particular this example does not establish a small-epsilon
counterexample.

Normalize an upward continuous normal to (t,1). Reflection in x allows
t>=0. Its actual buffered cap at Y is

    y+t x+a z+g(t)>=0,
    g(t)=(sqrt(1+19t^2/4)-1)/2.                            (4)

The term g is the full invariant norm contribution minus the marked
height 1/2. It is not a frozen Euclidean threshold approximation.

## 2. The unbuffered disjoint-core identity

For a through-origin nonvertical cap y+t x+a z>=0, decompose the actual
mixed set into the following disjoint pieces, ignoring null boundaries:

* the whole own rectangle K0, of volume10;
* equal central rectangles of width4,height2 at both bases -1,+1;
* equal central rectangles of width1,height2 at both bases -2,+2;
* the residual R1 at base -1: 2<=|x|<=5/2, |y|<=1;
* the residual R2 at base +2: 1/2<=|x|<=3/2, |y|<=1.

The first three pieces together are centrally symmetric about the
ambient origin and have total mass30. EVERY nonvertical through-origin
cap captures exactly15 of this core. Each residual is centrally
symmetric in its continuous coordinates, with volumes2 and4 respectively.
If a<=0, the residual R1 receives a nonnegative constant margin and
therefore contributes at least1. If a>=0, R2 contributes at least2.
Consequently the whole unbuffered cap mass F0 satisfies

    F0(t,a)>=16 for all a,t;
    F0(t,a)>=17 when a>=0.                                 (5)

These statements also hold for horizontal continuous normals, with
their actual corresponding base tilt. No whole fiber has been replaced
by a formal probability event.

## 3. A sharper elementary bound for small t

Assume 0<=t<=1/3 and a=-b<=0. Let R1(b),R2(b) denote the captured areas
of the two actual residual strips. For 0<=b<=1, no point of the first
strip has margin b+t x<=-1, because t|x|<=5/6. Only its positive-x half
can saturate at full height. Hence

    R1(b)=1+b-int_(2 to5/2)(b+t x-1)_+ dx
          >=1+b-(1/2)(b+5t/2-1)_+.                       (6)

For R2 no point has margin -2b+t x>=1, since t|x|<=1/2.
Its capture is the integral of (1-2b+t x)_+. Convexity of the positive
part and symmetry of its x-domain give

    R2(b)>=2(1-2b)_+.                                    (7)

On 0<=b<=1/2 the sum of the right sides in (6),(7) is decreasing in b;
on 1/2<=b<=1 it is increasing. Its minimum is therefore at b=1/2,
with value

    3/2-(5t/4-1/4)_+.

For b>=1, monotonicity of R1 and (6) at b=1 instead give
R1(b)>=2-5t/4>=19/12>3/2. Adding the exact core mass15 proves

    F0(t,a)>=33/2-(5t/4-1/4)_+,
                    a<=0, 0<=t<=1/3.                     (8)

## 4. The actual own-fiber buffer gain is monotone

Adding g(t) to every margin can only increase all captured fiber areas.
Let Delta0(t) be its increase on the own rectangle alone. For t>0,

    Delta0(t)=5 Pr{|X+Y/t|<=g(t)/t},                       (9)

where X,Y are independent uniform variables on [-5/2,5/2] and [-1,1].
This follows by central symmetry, since the own rectangle has area10.
The function g(t)/t is strictly increasing. For every fixed h>=0 the
function v -> Pr{|X+v|<=h} is even and nonincreasing in |v|, by the
interval-overlap formula. Thus replacing Y/t by the smaller symmetric
noise at a larger t increases the probability in (9). Enlarging the
threshold g(t)/t also increases it. Therefore Delta0 is nondecreasing
on t>0. This proof uses actual uniform rectangle marginals.

At t=1/5 and t=1/3 the entire moved own strip remains in the constant
section-density part: g(t)+(5/2)t<=1. Its gain is then exactly5g(t), so

    Delta0(1/5)=(sqrt(119)-10)/4 >1/6,
    Delta0(1/3)=5(sqrt(55)-6)/12 >1/2.                    (10)

The strict comparisons reduce respectively to1071>1024 and1375>1296.
For every t>0, Delta0(t)>0.

## 5. All upward, downward, horizontal and pure-base caps

Let F(t,a) be the buffered mass in (4). It is at least F0(t,a)+Delta0(t).
If a>=0, (5) already gives F>=17. For a<0:

* When 0<t<=1/5, (8) gives F0>=33/2, and Delta0>0.
* When 1/5<=t<=1/3, the possible deficit in (8) is at most1/6,
  strictly paid by (10) and monotonicity.
* When t>=1/3, (5) gives F0>=16, and (10) pays strictly more than1/2.

Thus EVERY t>0 gives mass STRICTLY GREATER than33/2, uniformly in a
pointwise as stated. This is an all-direction proof, not a numerical
screen or a finite list of selected normals.

At t=0, g=0. For a=-b<0 direct interval clipping gives

    F(0,-b)=18-3b,      0<=b<=1/2;
             16+b,      1/2<=b<=1;
             17,        b>=1.                            (11)

For a>=0 use (5). Hence the unique upward minimizing parameters are
t=0,a=-1/2, and the mass is33/2.

A downward continuous normal is reduced by y-reflection to the same
formula, but with added constant (sqrt(1+19t^2/4)+1)/2, one larger than
g(t). All such caps dominate their upward counterpart. If that upward
counterpart is not the unique minimum, its mass is already strictly
larger. At the unique minimum the additional unit margin strictly
increases own capture from5 to10. Thus no downward cap attains33/2.

For a horizontal continuous normal, reflect x and normalize its positive
component to1. The physical buffer shift is sqrt(19)/4. By (5) the
unbuffered mass is at least16, and the own area gain is exactly
sqrt(19)/2>1/2, since sqrt(19)/4<5/2. These caps are also strictly larger.

Finally the two closed pure-base caps at source base0 have masses22 and24
(and the zero normal has mass36). A threshold farther outward than the
minimal containing buffered threshold cannot reduce captured volume.
At the sole minimizing minimal threshold, its own trace is proper, so
any strict outward relaxation adds a positive own-fiber strip.
All closed ambient cap orientations have now been included.

## 6. The unique cap and the surviving inside branch

The fixed-mark buffered depth is exactly

    Q=33/2,  Q/M=11/24,

and its unique minimizing ambient halfspace, up to positive scaling, is

    H={y-z/2>=0}.                                        (12)

Its own source trace y=0 is proper. At base -2 it has the INSIDE
supporting facet y=-1 of length1; at base +2 it has the OUTSIDE
supporting facet y=1 of length3. Every other trace is proper. Since
the minimizing halfspace is unique, there is NO inside-free minimizing
replacement at this fixed mark, even allowing all ambient normals.

For example the integer-tilt right derivatives at (12) are3 in the
positive direction and1 in the negative direction. They retain the
proper base moment -5+4=-1, inside loss2 and outside gain6 with their
actual signs. This is consistent with the buffered zonoid theorem.

The example is strictly nonheavy and lattice complete, but is safely
above the OC target and is not claimed to be globally deepest, a joint
minimizer, or a small-epsilon limit. It blocks unconditional
inside-removability at a proper fixed mark. It leaves any stronger
selection using additional extremal or asymptotic premises separate.

Supplementary exact checker:
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_five_rectangle_inside_facet_two_sided.py`, **47,698 checks PASS**.
It verifies the exact core decomposition, all strip formulas, a rational
parametrization of the invariant norm, the source energy, unique axial
tilt, and supporting derivatives. The analytic cases in Sections3–5,
rather than numerical sampling, establish the all-normal result.
